newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's central bank chief beats Greenspan on pay.
newsitem.headline: Japan's central bank chief beats Greenspan on pay.

text.p: Maybe Alan Greenspan should change jobs and move to Japan.

Figures released on Wednesday showed Greenspan's counterpart in Tokyo, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita, had an annual salary three times greater than that of the man credited with guiding the United States to its present boom while Japan's economy stood still.
In the first ever disclosure of BOJ executives' salaries, Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) submitted data to parliament showing Matsushita earned 51.33 million yen ($424,000) in 1996.

U.S. media have reported, based on data received under the Freedom of Information Act, that Greenspan's salary in 1995 as chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve was just $133,600. Salary details for last year were unavailable.

At that salary, the man described as the most powerful person in world finance earned only half of what each of the seven directors of the BOJ made in 1996 as they struggled to get the Japanese economy back on track and saw the yen sink against the dollar.
Greenspan was also poorly paid compared with top executives of Japan's major banks, which are saddled with mammoth bad loans.
The average annual income for executives at the banks was 29.7 million yen ($245,000), nearly twice Greenspan's salary.
The BOJ's Matsushita need not rely only on his salary when he is done with his labours.
The MOF figures showed that when his five-year term ends in 1999 he can look forward to a lump sum retirement payout of some 75 million yen ($619,000). ($1=121 yen)
